claims.text: Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in a simple single-phase solid-solution state has relatively low hardness.
Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in a simple single-phase solid-solution state has relatively low compressive strength.
The homogeneous crystal structure of single-phase CoCrFeNiTi has low lattice friction.
Single-phase CoCrFeNiTi contains few intrinsic obstacles to dislocation motion and lacks nanoscale obstacles or ordered domains.
Low lattice friction and a low density of intrinsic obstacles permit easy dislocation glide.
Easy dislocation glide causes the relatively low hardness and strength attributed to the starting alloy.
The absence of nanoscale obstacles or ordered domains accounts for the favorable plasticity and machinability of the starting alloy.
Secondary phases, precipitates, or short-range ordered domains impede dislocation glide and thereby increase strength and hardness.
Arc melting and homogenization can produce homogeneous, single-phase equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
The proposed single phase is likely either FCC or BCC.
Aging equimolar CoCrFeNiTi at approximately 650 °C for several hours followed by rapid quenching can induce nanoscale precipitation or short-range ordering.
The induced precipitates or ordered domains will act as dislocation-pinning centers.
The aged alloy will have higher yield stress, compressive strength, and microhardness than the untreated baseline.
The strengthening treatment may produce a modest reduction in ductility.
The proposed mechanism applies from 25 °C to approximately 600 °C under low-to-moderate strain-rate compression or microindentation conditions.
Outside the proposed temperature and loading limits, precipitate coarsening or dynamic recovery may become dominant.

contradictions.description: The outcome describes ductility loss only as a potential consequence, whereas the falsification rule treats failure to observe reduced ductility as grounds for falsification. This makes an optional prediction into a required result even though obstacle strengthening could occur without a measurable ductility decrease.
